Debiased scan for the difference of two portfolio means

Source: R/scan_contrast.R
sharp_scan_mean_contrast.Rd

sharp_scan_mean_contrast() is sharp_scan_contrast() for an outcome that is not binary: it compares the means of two disjoint portfolios chosen by \(X\) under the assumption of sharp_scan_mean(), with each endpoint estimated by sharp_scan_mean_ci(). The sharp set for \(A - B\) is \([\mathrm{lower}_A - \mathrm{upper}_B,\ \mathrm{upper}_A - \mathrm{lower}_B]\); because the targets are disjoint, the standard error of each endpoint is the root of the sum of the squared standard errors of the arms. By default each target is a whole segment of rows, observed and unobserved alike; among = "unobserved" compares the means of the missing outcomes of the two segments, \(E(Y \mid R = 0)\) in each.

Usage

sharp_scan_mean_contrast(
  q,
  r,
  response,
  outcome,
  target_a,
  target_b,
  lambda = seq(0, 2, length.out = 81),
  weights = NULL,
  threshold = 0,
  level = 0.9,
  trim = 0,
  r_bounds = c(0.01, 0.99),
  labels = c("A", "B"),
  among = c("all", "unobserved")
)

Arguments

q

An \(n \times K\) matrix of conditional quantiles of \(Y\) given \(R = 1, X = x_i\) for every row, fitted out of fold, at the levels \((k - 1/2)/K\).

r

Cross-fitted \(\hat r(x_i)\) for every row, in (0, 1].

response

Response indicator for every row, 0/1 or logical.

outcome

Outcome; ignored (and may be NA) where response is 0.

target_a, target_b

Logical vectors, one per row, selecting the two portfolios by \(X\). They must be disjoint and non-empty.

lambda

Grid of \(\lambda\) values; must include 0.

weights

Optional non-negative row weights, a function of \(X\).

threshold

The difference at which the decision changes. Default 0.

level

Confidence level. Default 0.9.

trim

Rows with \(\hat r <\) trim leave the target. Default 0.

r_bounds

\(\hat r\) is clipped into this range before use. Default c(0.01, 0.99). The number of clipped target rows is reported, below and above apart: clipping at the top only stabilises the cap \(\pi \le 1\) for rows that are almost always observed, clipping at the bottom limits inverse weights.

labels

Names of the two portfolios, for printing and plotting.

among

"all" (default) or "unobserved", as in sharp_scan_contrast().

Value

An object of class c("sharp_scan_contrast", "sharp_scan_ci", "sharp_scan") as from sharp_scan_contrast(), with of_means = TRUE.

See also

sharp_scan_contrast(), sharp_scan_mean_ci(), crossfit_quantiles()

Examples

d <- simulate_shadow(3000, tilt = -1, outcome = "continuous", seed = 3)
q <- obs_quantiles(d, K = 50)   # the true quantile grids of the simulation
k <- sharp_scan_mean_contrast(q, d$obs_rate, d$observed, d$y,
                               target_a = d$x1 > 0, target_b = d$x1 <= 0,
                               lambda = seq(0, 2, length.out = 21),
                               labels = c("x1 > 0", "x1 <= 0"))
k
#> <sharp_scan_contrast> difference of means x1 > 0 - x1 <= 0, debiased, with 90% confidence set
#>   rows: 3000   x1 > 0: 1507 rows   x1 <= 0: 1493 rows
#>   clipped: 5 rows entering the sets with r-hat below 0.01, 0 above 0.99
#>   r-hat < 0.01: 5 target rows, 0 observed rows; smallest r-hat observed 0.025
#>   lambda = 0: 1.21 [1.05, 1.37]
#>   lambda = 2 (propensity ratio 7.39): set [-0.41, 2.74], confidence set [-0.599, 2.92]
#>   difference 0 reached by
#>     estimated set:        lambda = 1.45 (propensity ratio 4.26) 
#>     confidence set:       lambda = 1.24 (propensity ratio 3.44) 
#>     outer band (plug-in): lambda = 1.64 (propensity ratio 5.15) 
plot(k)
